population.span: STAREE enrolled people aged ≥70 years from 1583 general practices across Australia with no history of clinical cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or dementia.

endpoint.span: a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction or stroke, or coronary revascularization (to assess effects on major cardiovascular events)

treatment_strategy.span: Participants will be randomly assigned to oral atorvastatin (40 mg daily) or matching placebo (1:1 ratio).

follow_up.span: After a median of 5.9 years, a primary cardiovascular event had occurred

absent_reason: analysis_set: The protocol specifies planned intention-to-treat comparisons, but the held results abstracts do not state the analysis population actually used for this estimate.
served_mismatch: The served HR and confidence limits match the results abstract. However, served_outcome.estimand specifies RR, whereas the reported effect is HR; the served ITT label is not confirmed by the results abstracts.

entry_population_matches_question.why: The whole trial enrolled adults aged ≥70 years without clinical cardiovascular disease; additional exclusions narrow the eligible population within the question.
entry_population_matches_question.span: STAREE enrolled people aged ≥70 years from 1583 general practices across Australia with no history of clinical cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or dementia.

notes: The effect and follow-up are bound from the results abstract. Its endpoint includes coronary revascularization, consistent with the registry but absent from the earlier protocol and baseline-paper endpoint definitions. The results-specific definition is retained. The protocol describes initial 20 mg daily dosing for four weeks before escalation to 40 mg, with dose reduction or interruption permitted.
